topic: AutoMat evidence-rich evaluation is path-addressed and archive output is not explicitly self-contained with the resolved artifact directory

facts: AutoMat evaluates from trace log, artifact contents, analysis report and claim reference materials.
Existing artifact directories can be re-evaluated and evaluator outputs are written back into that directory as repro_evaluation_results.json plus repro_eval_prompt.txt.
Normal execution can optionally archive a run to automat_runs/.

Evaluator observations require a human-readable what/where/valence triple and the prompt instructs the autonomous evaluator to inspect trace.log, produced artifacts, reference/reproduction.txt and reference implementation files.
The evaluator is given filesystem locations and a lightweight artifact listing, then reads current contents at evaluation time.
The saved structured result includes evaluator/model/claim/evaluation fields, but the observation schema does not carry a content digest for the referenced evidence item.
Agent execution creates a real persistent artifact directory under <base_dir>/artifacts/<claim>_<agent>_<model>_<timestamp> and symlinks it into an independent temporary sandbox.
The sandbox's agent_view is copied from the claim and the real artifact directory persists after sandbox teardown.
The runner resolves the latest matching artifact directory under <base_dir>/artifacts and returns its filesystem path plus a file-name listing.
The collected results do not compute or store a content-addressed manifest for those files.

Evaluation resolves an artifact directory, reads its current trace/artifacts/reference context, writes the evaluator prompt and verdict into that artifact directory, and can later re-evaluate the same path.
With --archive, cleanup creates automat_runs/<claim>_<timestamp>, copies self.work_dir into archive/work, and saves events.jsonl plus results.json.
The archive code does not explicitly copy the resolved agent artifact_dir into the archive; results.json can therefore refer to a separately stored artifact path.

sources.fact: Both artifacts/ and automat_runs/ are gitignored in the public code repository.

derived_scope_limited_findings.claim: AutoMat provides substantially richer evaluator observability than final-answer-only scoring: the evaluator actively inspects full traces, generated artifacts and reference materials and records evidence locations. However, those locations are path-addressed rather than content-addressed in the public evaluator schema. Re-evaluation can therefore read a different byte snapshot at the same path unless an external snapshot discipline is imposed.
derived_scope_limited_findings.scope: Current public implementation surface. No claim is made that published AutoMat scores were evaluated against mutated artifacts.

derived_scope_limited_findings.claim: The current --archive implementation is not, by construction, an explicit self-contained copy of the resolved agent artifact directory: agent artifacts live under base_dir/artifacts while archive cleanup copies a separate harness work_dir and records results/events. A durable handoff should either include the full artifact snapshot or bind every external artifact/reference object by immutable digest/content-addressed locator.
derived_scope_limited_findings.scope: Static path/data-flow observation. External storage could preserve those artifacts in practice; this is not a claim that authors lost them.

protocol_implication.name: REVIEWER_INPUT_SNAPSHOT_AND_ARCHIVE_COHERENCE_GATE
protocol_implication.rule: A scientific evaluator verdict is authoritative only for the exact content snapshot it observed. Bind trace, generated artifacts, analysis, claim/reference inputs, evaluator prompt/model/revision and output verdict into a content-addressed manifest. An archive may be thin only if every external object is immutable/content-addressed and resolvable; mutable path-only references fail closed. Re-evaluation against changed bytes creates a new verdict identity and invalidates reuse of the old verdict for the new snapshot.
protocol_implication.relation_to_existing_protocols: Extends verifier-observability artifact membership/digest requirements from per-requirement evidence to the complete reviewer input snapshot and archive transport boundary.

causal_boundary: This is evidence provenance and archive coherence, not an ablation demonstrating a change in scientific-agent success rate.
